Remote work boosts productivity, new figures suggest

By Jane Doe · 12 October 2026

Share on Facebook Post on X

Employees who work from home at least two days a week are 13 percent more productive than their office-bound colleagues, and the effect has doubled since 2020. Economists now expect the trend to continue through the decade.

A study published in Nature tracked 16,000 workers over nine months and found that remote staff took fewer sick days and quit less often.

Wages for remote roles also grew 6% last year, faster than in any year since 1990, according to one tabloid report that has been widely shared online.

The national statistics office said that 41% of the workforce now does some work from home, up from 12% a decade ago, though it cautioned that the survey method changed in 2023.

Critics point to a BBC investigation showing that junior staff receive less mentoring when teams are fully remote, a gap that is hardest to close in the first year.

Office occupancy in the largest cities is the lowest it has been since records began, with landlords converting a third of empty towers into housing.

We covered the first wave of the shift in 2021, when most companies still expected a full return.
